thread:
incident-bot: PAGERS 🚨 metering-alert-high-delta triggered for billing-prod • severity: P2 • affected-service: metering-aggregator • runbook: /runbooks/metering-drift

sam: oncall here, getting the pager. seeing alerts about token-count drift between aggregator and the auth service.

arya: confirmed, dashboards show aggregator counts ~8-12% higher for a handful of accounts starting ~00:12 UTC. looks correlated with a retry loop in the ingest-forwarder ks.

chris: can you paste the query you ran?

arya: copied: ```SELECT account_id, sum(tokens) as agg_tokens, last_reported_tokens FROM meter_agg WHERE ts >= '2026-03-14T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 20;```

arya: quick snippet shows accounts A123, B987, and C444 spike. diff = agg_tokens - last_reported_tokens.

sam: any recent deploys to metering-aggregator?

evan: runtime team did a config push to continuous-batch-size on metering-aggregator yesterday to improve throughput. deploy was at 2026-03-13 23:50 UTC and rolled to 3/3 nodes. No immediate alerts then.

liz: support FYI — we have one active customer ticket complaining about unexpected overage flags. Customer claims they were charged for tokens that never showed in their app.

billing-bot: ALERT: overage-flag emitted for account A123 at 00:17 UTC — rule: threshold:monthly_tokens > committed_limit * 1.05

sam: ok — priority now: 1) stop further incorrect counting / overage flags, 2) mitigate customer-facing alerts, 3) run reconciliation and rollback if necessary.

chris: propose immediate mitigation: disable the new batching config (hotfix) on aggregator to stop the drift and fallback to previous config. It should be safe and low-risk.

evan: I can revert config and restart aggregator pods in next 3 min. Will use `kubectl patch` to avoid full redeploy. Command: ```kubectl -n prod set env deploy/metering-aggregator BATCH_SIZE=64 --overwrite``` then rolling restart.

sam: do it. annotate the change in the incident timeline.

evan: patching now. 1/3 pods restarted.

arya: while that's going, I'm running a streaming check to compare pre- and post-restart token diffs. running `metering-verify --live-compare --window 10m`

evan: all pods restarted. health checks passed.

arya: early signs: new counts are aligning closer to auth service for the last 5 minutes. diff dropped from ~10% to ~0.8% for sample accounts.

sam: good. liz, can you pause auto-generated overage emails for the affected rule?

liz: yep pausing now in the billing console. toggled `auto_overage_notifications` -> false for rule:monthly_tokens. took a screenshot: https://redwood.internal/screenshots/1955009876/pause.png :thumbsup:

billing-bot: INFO: paused overage notifications for rule monthly_tokens at 00:29 UTC by liz

arya: starting a reconciliation job to reprocess the ingestion window 00:00-00:30 UTC and generate corrected aggregates. this will run as backfill job `backfill-metrics-1955009876`. estimate ~12m.

chris: we should mark customer-impact and kick off customer comms. sam, want to own the incident lead narrative?

sam: i'll draft an initial postmortem summary and customer-facing blurb. high level: transient token-count drift due to batching config, resulted in spurious overage flags for a subset of customers. mitigation: reverted config, paused notifications, backfill running, recon in progress.

liz: I'll open a CS triage ticket and link to the incident thread and affected accounts. ticket: CS-7182. Adding template message for customers: "We observed a metering inconsistency that may have triggered overage notifications; we have paused notifications and are reconciling usage. No billing charges will be finalized until reconciliation completes."

evan: backfill job started. logs: ```[00:32:12] backfill-metrics-1955009876: started
[00:34:05] reprocess account A123: delta corrected -1200 tokens
[00:35:18] reprocess account B987: delta corrected -450 tokens```

arya: recon progress now at ~60%. expected finish in ~6m. storing per-account correction deltas to s3://metering-recon/1955009876/deltas.csv

sam: question: do we need to revert any billing calculations already exported to billing downstream?

chris: billing export runs hourly. last export was 00:00 UTC, next is 01:00. Corrections are in our backfill artifacts; we should prevent the 01:00 export if corrections incomplete to avoid publishing wrong numbers.

liz: on it — setting billing-export hold for the 01:00 job. billing pipeline triggered hold by tag `incident-1955009876`.
